'''Jalebi''' is a sweet [[Cookbook:Fritter|fritter]] that is shaped like a slightly large, chaotic pretzel. It is traditionally prepared in [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|India]] and [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Pakistan|Pakistan]]. Well-made jalebi has a tart element with a sweet taste.

==Ingredients==
===Batter===
* 3 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Besan|gram flour]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
* 1½ cups [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* 3 cups of vegetable [[Cookbook:Oil|oil/ghee]] for [[Cookbook:Deep Fat Frying|deep frying]]

===Syrup===
* 4 cups white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 3 cups water
* ⅛ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Cream of Tartar|cream of tartar]]
* Red and yellow [[Cookbook:Food Coloring|food colorings]]
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Rosewater|rosewater]]

==Procedure==
# Mix up the batter ingredients until smooth.
# Let the batter sit unrefrigerated and uncovered overnight (about 12 hours).
# Mix the sugar, water, and cream of tartar for the syrup.
# Stir the syrup over moderate heat until the sugar is dissolved.
# Put on high heat and boil for 5 minutes. 
# Let the syrup cool, and stir in the rosewater. Use food coloring to tint it light orange.
# Put the vegetable oil in a wide [[Cookbook:Wok|wok]]-like dish, and heat to about 350°F (175°C).
# Put the batter into a [[Cookbook:Pastry Bag|pastry bag]] with about a ¼ [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] opening. If it is too dry to squeeze out, mix in a bit of water.
# Squeeze the batter into the oil, making a couple of figure-eight shapes and loops on top of each other. The shape should be about 3 inches on its longest side.
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] each jalebi until golden brown. Remove, let the oil drain off, then soak in syrup for a minute.
# Serve.
